qs.q:
Pocket Money — Which person…

A=Anna Marie (youngest of 3 sisters, sisters stole her money, hid it from them)
B=Burt (locked it in special box, too precious to spend, now regrets not spending it on fun)
C=Collin (only mate with pocket money, paid for outings, close friendships formed)
D=Dianne (waited eagerly for Fridays, ran to shop, bought sweets/chocolates, happiest memories)
E=Ellen (parents gave less than her mates, had to be selective about music, learned value of money)
F=Frederick (only kid with pocket money in poor neighbourhood, hid what he bought, didn't want to stand out)

0. felt they did not have enough pocket money? [E=Ellen]
1. saved their pocket money?
2. shared their pocket money?
3. spent their pocket money quickly?
4. spent their pocket money on going out?
5. bought food with their pocket money?
6. bought records with their pocket money?
7. did not receive regular pocket money?
8. looked forward to getting their pocket money?
9. now regrets what they did with their pocket money?
10. says having pocket money helped them later?
11. felt embarrassed about their pocket money?
12. hid their pocket money?
items: 4 — spent their pocket money on going out?
5 — bought food with their pocket money?
6 — bought records with their pocket money?
7 — did not receive regular pocket money?
8 — looked forward to getting their pocket money?
9 — now regrets what they did with their pocket money?
10 — says having pocket money helped them later?
11 — felt embarrassed about their pocket money?

Working with Whales

"What amazed me, however, was how, despite its size, it looked so ELEGANT as it swam by."

What did the author find so surprising about his first meeting with a whale?
A How beautifully the whale moved.
B How curious the whale was.
C How close the whale came.
D How big the whale was.

Working with Whales

"I knew, there and then, what I wanted to do with my life."

According to the author, why was the trip in paragraph one so important?
A He had never realised how curious whales were.
B It was the first time he had seen a whale.
C He was actually able to touch the whale.
D It helped him to choose his profession.
opts: He had never realised how curious whales were.
It was the first time he had seen a whale.
He was actually able to touch the whale.
It helped him to choose his profession.

Working with Whales

"I'm a scientist, and what attracts me is that there is STILL SO MUCH ABOUT THEM THAT WE DON'T KNOW."

C Because there are so many different kinds.
D Because of the fact they are so enormous.

Because of the way they behave in groups.
Because there are so many different kinds.
Because of the fact they are so enormous.

Is There Anything Out There?

B We have been able to find planets that are big and hot.
C However, it's rather slow on a cosmic scale.
D This is quite an impressive number.
E But this will take some time to do.
F They seem very, very small.
G They can't see you and me.
H It's a long, long way.
opts: A — A lot of nothingness until the next bit of something.
B — We have found planets that are big and hot.
C — However, it's rather slow on a cosmic scale.
D — This is quite an impressive number.
E — But this will take some time to do.
F — They seem very, very small.
G — They can't see you and me.
H — It's a long, long way.
